documents.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is transforming academic writing and research, creating an urgent need for prompt literacy as a core competency in higher education. This chapter develops an integrated framework that positions prompt literacy as a cognitive, pedagogical, and ethical capability supporting responsible human–AI collaboration. Drawing on contemporary scholarship, this chapter synthesises existing literature to examine prompt design, evaluation, research applications, instructional strategies, and ethical governance. It further proposes a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) verification framework to strengthen transparency, academic integrity, and the reliability of AI-assisted scholarship. This chapter contributes a structured conceptual model that informs curriculum design, research training, assessment practices, and institutional policy, enabling higher education institutions to foster responsible, critical, and future-ready AI-enabled scholarship.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The chapter examines the role of prompt literacy as a structured academic competence in AI-supported writing and research within higher education. It develops and empirically tests a conceptual framework linking prompt quality to academic writing and research performance through the mediating role of cognitive engagement and the moderating influence of institutional academic integrity orientation. Drawing on cognitive, academic literacy, metacognitive, and socio-technical perspectives, the chapter demonstrates that effective prompting is not merely technical but central to scholarly practice. Findings indicate that high-quality prompts enhance analytical depth, coherence, and methodological clarity, particularly when users actively engage with AI outputs. Furthermore, institutional integrity environments strengthen responsible AI use and amplify performance outcomes. The chapter contributes theoretical, pedagogical, and policy insights by positioning prompt literacy as essential for sustaining academic rigor in AI-mediated scholarship.

Introduction Psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation play an important role in academic engagement, professional identity development, and commitment to the teaching profession. However, limited evidence is available on how employment status, reasons for enrolment, and early vocational orientation are jointly associated with these constructs among students in initial teacher education. This study examined psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation among postgraduate students enrolled in Master's Degree programmes in Secondary Teacher Education. Methods A total of 239 postgraduate students enrolled at the University of Castilla-La Mancha and Villanueva University (Spain) participated in the study. Participants completed Ryff's Psychological Well-Being Scale and the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI). Independent-samples t-tests were conducted to examine differences in psychological well-being and intrinsic motivation according to employment status, reasons for enrolment, and early teaching vocation. Results No statistically significant differences in psychological well-being were observed according to employment status or reason for enrolment. Students who were not actively seeking employment reported significantly higher scores on Interest/Enjoyment and Perceived Choice, as well as a higher overall IMI score, than those actively seeking employment, whereas no significant differences were found for Value/Usefulness. Reason for enrolment was also associated with specific aspects of intrinsic motivation: participants who enrolled for reasons other than employment-related motives reported significantly higher Perceived Choice and overall IMI scores, while no significant differences emerged for Interest/Enjoyment or Value/Usefulness. The most consistent differences were associated with early teaching vocation. Students who had identified teaching as a professional goal from the beginning of their university studies reported significantly higher scores across all IMI dimensions ( p < .001) and a significantly higher score for Purpose in Life ( p < .001). Discussion These findings highlight early vocational orientation as a particularly relevant factor in understanding motivational engagement and professional purpose during initial teacher education. They also underscore the importance of considering both vocational and contextual factors when designing teacher education experiences that support professional identity development and sustained engagement with the teaching profession.

Military work environments combine high operational demands, hierarchical control and limited autonomy, creating conditions in which psychosocial risks may affect occupational health. This study examined an integrated psychosocial occupational health model linking job stress, distributive justice, psychological capital, military identity and occupational health outcomes among Spanish enlisted military personnel. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 382 enlisted members of the Spanish Armed Forces between February 17 and March 30, 2025. Measures assessed job stress, distributive justice, psychological capital, military identity, well-being, job satisfaction and work engagement. Direct and indirect associations were estimated using partial least squares structural equation modelling with 10,000 bootstrap samples. Job stress was negatively associated with psychological capital, distributive justice, military identity and occupational health outcomes. Psychological capital and military identity were positively associated with occupational health outcomes, and the model explained 73.5% of their variance. Indirect effects indicated that job stress was associated with poorer occupational health mainly through lower psychological capital and, to a lesser extent, lower military identity. The findings suggest that occupational health in military work environments is associated not only with job stress but also with personal, organisational and identity-related resources. Psychosocial risk prevention in military and other hierarchical workplaces may benefit from combining stressor reduction with strategies that strengthen psychological capital, distributive fairness and constructive occupational identity.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to draft the news. These systems may frame the news differently from human journalists. In particular, it remains less understood how they handle metaphor, a potent framing tool in news discourse. Following Bourdieu’s field theory, we compare LLMs’ metaphorical framing with the journalistic habitus of human reporting in two studies of German news on Chinese investment spanning a quarter century (with 2975 metaphors from human journalism and 1924 from LLM-generated news writing), and conduct a prompting experiment across four instructions and three recent LLMs (DeepSeek V4, GPT-5.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5) with 4877 metaphors. We find that compared to journalists that favored deliberate, evaluatively charged figurative expressions, the LLM-generated news was conventional by default, framing investment as a procedural, depoliticized process. We regard this disposition as a “machine habitus”. It proved durable across prompted years and model versions, bound to a closed set of source domains, and generative , varying under instruction only within that set. Its conceptual sources and deliberateness moved sharply with the prompt, yet showed little variation across LLMs, while its evaluative orientation tracked the prompt, with only weak differences by model origin. Across two versions of LLMs, the disposition proved more durable than the volume of metaphor it governs: the newer LLMs wrote more figuratively yet remained conflict-averse. The study contributes to debates on automation, framing, and accountability in journalism.

Artificial intelligence and digitally mediated creative practices are changing not only the tools available to teachers but also the conditions under which teachers exercise professional judgment. Although posthuman scholarship offers a rich vocabulary for understanding relational agency among humans, technologies, materials, and environments, its educational implications often remain philosophically expansive and pedagogically underspecified. This study therefore refined an initial conceptual framework of Posthuman Aesthetic Pedagogy for teacher education through multidisciplinary expert consultation. The study used a theory-informed qualitative design rather than an inductive theory-generation approach. Five expert fields spanning art education, curriculum studies, educational philosophy, media aesthetics, and contemporary artistic practice critically examined the framework's coherence, educational relevance, conceptual relations, and implications. Consultation data were interpreted recursively in relation to the initial framework through three analytic lenses: conceptual confirmation, conceptual divergence, and conceptual refinement. Experts broadly confirmed the value of relationality, mediation, dialogicity, transformative creativity, and reflective responsibility, while questioning any account that treated technology as a neutral tool, aesthetic experience as private appreciation, or creativity as unconstrained novelty. The refined framework consequently positions professional judgment as the connective pedagogical capacity through which future teachers notice distributed agency, interpret technologically mediated situations, deliberate with others, create alternatives, and assume responsibility for educational consequences. The contribution is threefold: conceptually, the study clarifies the internal relations of Posthuman Aesthetic Pedagogy; methodologically, it demonstrates how expert consultation can refine rather than falsely “validate” a theory-informed framework; and educationally, it offers a teacher-education orientation that complements competency frameworks by foregrounding situated, aesthetic, ethical judgment. Although it requires empirical examination in teacher-education settings, this framework provides a defensible basis for designing learning experiences in which teachers critically and creatively negotiate complex human-technology relations.

Abstract Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing scientific discovery in medicine, with reinforcement learning (RL) emerging as a promising tool for optimizing therapeutic strategies. Yet applying RL to complex scenarios such as therapy dynamics in solid tumors is constrained by the challenge of constructing training environments that are both computationally efficient and mechanistically interpretable. Here, we introduce Reinforcement Failing, an AI-guided, human-in-the-loop discovery framework that shifts the focus from agent policy optimization to the refinement of the training environment itself. By combining multi-fidelity RL with group-relative performance evaluation across agent cohorts, Reinforcement Failing systematically reveals emergent mechanisms that first-principles models overlook. We apply this framework to adaptive therapy in solid tumors, which seeks to delay resistance-mediated treatment failure. In this setting, Reinforcement Failing uncovered a coupling between the mechanically driven collective motion of cells and spatially-heterogeneous proliferation that strongly influences therapy outcomes. We integrated these emergent physical mechanisms with existing domain knowledge into an augmented training environment, resulting in improved cross-environment therapeutic performance and exposure of potential pitfalls during translation. More broadly, these findings position Reinforcement Failing as a powerful artificial scientific discovery framework, capable of deciphering high-complexity processes at the interface of physics, machine learning, and medicine.

Culture, morals, and religion have always been a part of parenting, and certain cultural, moral, and religious beliefs shape parents' approach to nurturing the emotional, intellectual, social, and spiritual growth of their children. Still, the role and context in which parents carry out their responsibilities have dramatically changed in recent years with the rise of digital technologies such as the smartphone, social media, artificial intelligence, online games, streaming services, virtual learning environments and internet-based communications. In today's world, religious parents are tasked with taking both risks and benefits of the new technologies which offer learning and development opportunities to children, while at the same time safeguarding them from the dangers the Internet holds that might undermine their religious beliefs, morals, and ethics. In this way, religion-based parenting has become a dynamic process that combines traditional religious values and teachings.

With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), the research findings suggest that users may form romantic relationship with AI and the individuals with varying attachment styles may turn to AI as a substitute to obtain emotional fulfillment typically derived from human relationships. However, few studies have explored why users fall in love with AI. Therefore, this research collect data based on Chinese Adaption of Experiences in Close Relationship Scale (ECR) and online questionnaire. Using the Pearson correlations analysis, the study determines the connection between AI romance willingness and attachment types. The study's findings indicate a strong positive relationship between AI romance willingness and the degree of attachment anxiety or attachment avoidance. AI romance willingness is positively correlated with an individual's attachment avoidance and anxiety levels. The result not only broadens the explanatory scope of the attachment theory but also provides certain feasibility for AI virtual lovers. However the study neither compared AI romance willingness across secure, anxious and avoidant attachment groups, nor employed a sample with sufficient representativeness to support the generalizable conclusions.

Smart workflow automation (SWA) — encompassing robotic process automation (RPA), AI driven process mining, low-code/no-code (LCNC) platforms, and cognitive or hyperautomation systems — has emerged as one of the fastest-growing research domains at the intersection of computer science, management information systems, and industrial engineering. This paper presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of SWA research published between 2012 and 2023, drawing on 2,847 peer-reviewed documents retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library. Using co-citation analysis, keyword co-occurrence mapping, and citation trend modeling performed in VOSviewer and Bibliometrix, five major thematic clusters are identified: RPA and bot-based automation, AI/ML-driven process mining, low-code/no-code platforms, workflow orchestration and business process management (BPM), and cognitive/intelligent automation. The analysis reveals that while traditional RPA and BPM literature exhibits mature, steady citation growth, AI-driven process mining and low-code/no-code platforms demonstrate the highest annual growth rates, at 22.7% and 34.1% respectively, indicating a marked shift in research attention toward intelligent, accessible automation tooling. Scatter graph analysis of citation accumulation against publication year, and of keyword frequency against growth rate, provides quantitative confirmation of this thematic evolution. The findings offer researchers, practitioners, and funding bodies an evidence-based map of the SWA research landscape and identify under-explored intersections — particularly explainable AI in automation governance and human-in-the-loop hyperautomation — as priority directions for future investigation.Originally published in Journal of Computational Analysis and Applications, Volume 33, Issue 5 (2024), pages 3817–3829. Purpose Business education is stuck in outmoded ideas of business, the market and the world. We have known this for decades, but little has changed. As problems like climate change and inequality worsen, the challenge of creating responsible management education is not to find ways to integrate new electives into that outdated curriculum. The challenge is to fundamentally transform the curriculum, shedding some concepts, models and values while adding a new focus that properly reflects the powerful influence of business and inspires a new set of aspirational values through which business school graduates will be developed. Design/methodology/approach This is a Viewpoint essay, based on the author’s 30 years tenure as a professor in business education and research. In more recent years, the author has devoted his writing, speaking, research and teaching on reforming the curriculum and research norms to bring them more in line with the needs of the 21st century. Findings Too much attention in business education has been placed on the “how” of business, the tools in the core; not enough attention is devoted to “why” they will be deployed. This Viewpoint recommends (1) a re-envisioned core, (2) a focus outward on the role and purpose of business in society, (3) a focus inward on character, seeking to instill the notion of “management as a calling” and (4) an alignment of the supporting structures of the educational environment to reinforce a set of internally derived aspirational goals. Research limitations/implications This is a Viewpoint essay, and as such, is meant to stir debate and discussion over the future of business education. The real impact of this article will be measured, not by how often it is cited, but instead by how often it is used to stir change within the world’s business schools. Practical implications Business schools are facing numerous challenges from Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models to high tuition to questions over their value proposition. Today, society has serious questions about the role of business in society, and business students are asking for more from their business school experience, desiring content that reflects the challenges they will face. The proposals in this article are one professor’s views on how to address them. Social implications Businesses play an increasingly powerful role in addressing humanity’s challenges, but it’s not clear whether it will be a positive one. To be sure, businesses hold enormous powers of ideation, production and distribution to provide solutions to society’s problems at the scale we need them. They also hold the potential to multiply the effects of the darkest of human impulses and result in exploitation, materialism and greed. There is an urgent need to nurture a new breed of business leaders who view business not only as a means to profitability but also as a vehicle to serve society. Originality/value There are numerous calls for reforming business education, and this Viewpoint adds to that conversation. Some of the content is new and original, based on 30 years of teaching, writing and course development. Some of the content builds on and supports what others have discussed. Until there is real change, these arguments need to be restated, improved, amplified and applied when the institutions of academia are ready.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), especially the fast iteration and widespread deployment of large language models (LLMs), has ushered in a new paradigm for the intelligent augmentation of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems (ATS). By combining the powerful reasoning and generative capabilities of LLMs with the timeliness and accuracy of external knowledge bases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) has emerged as a highly promising approach to addressing knowledge-intensive challenges in the operation and maintenance of electronic test instruments. This paper presents a comprehensive review of RAG and its applications in the field of electronic test instruments. First, the basic architecture of RAG is reviewed, including retrieval mechanisms, knowledge-base construction, and generative models. Then, considering the operational characteristics of electronic test instruments and automatic test systems, key knowledge-intensive tasks are analyzed, such as fault diagnosis, test configuration, and process planning, followed by a discussion of representative RAG-based applications, including intelligent fault diagnosis systems, adaptive test-parameter configuration, and interactive question-answering assistants. In addition, practical considerations for engineering implementation are discussed with respect to knowledge-base construction and effectiveness evaluation. Finally, open issues and future research directions are outlined, including multimodal RAG, federated learning for distributed knowledge bases, and edge deployment. This review aims to provide researchers and practitioners in relevant industries with a comprehensive understanding of the current status and development prospects of RAG technologies in electronic test instruments.

Strategic management focuses on decisions shaping the future of businesses, while revenue management functions as a key strategic link within the value chain. In the tourism sector, traditional pricing approaches based on cost and demand have evolved due to the active role of guests in value creation. Perceived value, willingness to pay, and market positioning significantly influence pricing decisions, making it a multidimensional and multi-actor process. Therefore, relying solely on traditional indicators such as RevPAR, ADR, and occupancy rates is insufficient to explain today's strategic pricing logic. Although artificial intelligence and algorithmic systems enhance pricing efficiency, human judgment remains essential, especially in uncertain and crisis contexts. This chapter emphasizes the need to integrate analytical tools with managerial reasoning, offering a more holistic and strategic perspective on revenue management and pricing in accommodation businesses.

Coronary artery disease, driven by the progressive accumulation of atherosclerotic plaque within the epicardial coronary arteries, remains a leading cause of myocardial ischemia and global morbidity. A fundamental challenge in the clinical management of the disease has been the reliance on anatomic stenosis severity alone, a metric that frequently dissociates from the hemodynamic significance of a lesion and thus offers limited guidance for optimal revascularization. The advent of invasive measurements marked a transformative paradigm shift, enabling the development of a diverse functional indices for the evaluation of coronary physiology. Recently, the development of computational science and artificial intelligence has accelerated the translation of these physiological assessments into the non-invasive domain, primarily through high-fidelity numerical simulations and efficient machine learning algorithms. This review systematically examines the evolution of coronary functional assessment across several pivotal frontiers. It begins by contextualizing the diagnostic landscape prior to the widespread adoption of functional indices, where clinical decisions were predominantly informed by imaging-derived anatomical parameters. Subsequently, it traces the historical evolution of invasive coronary functional indices, critically evaluating the comparative effectiveness of pressure-derived metrics against flow-derived metrics in the detection of hemodynamically significant ischemia. Furthermore, a critical evaluation of emerging artificial intelligence methodologies for the non-invasive evaluation of functional significance were employed. By synthesizing these technological methodologies, this review aims to elucidate the appropriate clinical application of each functional index, thereby providing a road-map for clinicians to achieve precise, individualized ischemia evaluation and guide therapeutic decision-making in the contemporary era of precision cardiovascular medicine.

Repair and mechanical enterprises are characterized by heterogeneous technological processes that may expose workers simultaneously to physical, chemical, and ergonomic hazards. Conventional occupational hygiene approaches frequently assess individual hazards separately, which may underestimate the overall occupational burden when several exposures occur concurrently. Objective: To develop a scientifically grounded methodological framework for quantitative prioritization of combined occupational hazards in repair and mechanical enterprises and to define an analytical pathway for evaluating their relationship with workers' health. Materials and Methods: An analytical narrative review of contemporary occupational health literature was conducted with emphasis on multiple-exposure assessment, job-exposure matrices, occupational epidemiology, quantitative risk assessment, and prevention prioritization. PubMed-indexed studies, international occupational health evidence, and methodological recommendations from authoritative occupational safety institutions were considered. A multistage framework integrating exposure characterization, normalization against applicable occupational exposure limits, cumulative exposure profiling, interaction assessment, health-outcome modelling, and prevention prioritization was developed. Results: The proposed framework consists of five sequential components: (1) identification and characterization of workplace hazards; (2) quantitative estimation of individual exposure burden; (3) construction of a job–exposure profile; (4) statistical assessment of exposure–health relationships; and (5) prioritization of preventive interventions according to risk magnitude, preventability, and expected effectiveness. A normalized exposure ratio is proposed for individual hazards, while a weighted cumulative exposure score may be used for preliminary prioritization when methodological assumptions permit. For epidemiological analysis, multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms is recommended to distinguish independent and combined effects. The framework emphasizes that cumulative exposure should not be reduced to a simple arithmetic sum when hazards act through different biological pathways. Conclusion: Quantitative assessment of combined occupational hazards should move beyond isolated measurements toward an integrated exposure–health–prevention model. The proposed framework can provide a methodological basis for occupational hygiene studies in repair and mechanical enterprises and may support the development of evidence-based, prioritized health-improvement interventions.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: The education technology (Ed-Tech) industry is evolving rapidly thanks to the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI), which is now being used to personalize learning, automate evaluation, create intelligent content and manage student data and information, as well as streamline business operations. The rise of skills and technologies like AI is transforming the landscape of Ed-Tech startups in Uttar Pradesh by enhancing their competitive edge, reducing operational expenses, boosting user engagement, and optimizing educational delivery. This study focuses on the importance and contribution of Artificial Intelligence in the development and sustainability of the start-ups in the Ed-Tech sector in Uttar Pradesh. It emphasizes the ways in which AI aids companies in growing, enhancing their operations, innovating, pleasing customers, customizing learning, and staying sustainable over time. The study also reveals key challenges in the implementation of AI such as cost of implementation, lack of skilled expertise, privacy issues, technology constraints, and change resistance. Descriptive research design is proposed with the help of primary data collection from selected Ed-Tech start-ups and their employees/manager in UP. The analysis is based on percentages, looking at trends in AI use and impact on business performance and sustainability. The results of the study will benefit entrepreneurs, Ed-Tech managers, policy makers and others as they look for ways to implement AI effectively. The results could help in understanding the role of AI in promoting sustainable growth of the nascent Ed-Tech ecosystem in UP, if used responsibly and strategically
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: This article examines the role of human resource development in shaping an innovative environment for art in the context of accelerating digitalisation and global transformation in the 21st century. The relevance of the topic arises from the transition of creative industries from predominantly traditional forms of artistic activity toward technology-enabled and interdisciplinary models in which human capital becomes a central driver of new artistic forms, organisational adaptation, and wider socio-economic development. Drawing on 32 scholarly and institutional sources published mainly between 2021 and 2025 and accessed through academic repositories, publisher platforms, and institutional websites, the study explores the theoretical foundations, mechanisms of influence, and current practices of human resource management in the artistic and creative sectors. The findings indicate that strengthening human potential through competence-based development, digital learning, gamification, data-informed HR practices, artificial intelligence, creative clusters, and continuous professional development can support innovation capacity when these tools are aligned with artistic goals and organisational needs. Particular attention is given to developments in Russia while also drawing on international evidence concerning human capital, productivity, arts management, skills transformation, and workforce development. The article further proposes practical recommendations concerning competence-based assessment, investment in lifelong learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and international cooperation. Rather than treating technology as a substitute for artistic judgement, the study concludes that sustainable innovation in the arts depends on the combined development of creative, digital, analytical, collaborative, and adaptive capabilities.
topics: Innovations in Education and Learning Technologies

documents.abstract: This review synthesises historical scholarship on everyday life and social structure in the Russian Empire during the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, with a focus on peasant and worker communities between the emancipation of 1861 and the revolutions of 1917. The first part examines daily life: birth, childhood and family; food and drink; clothing, housing and household goods; markets and consumption; education and literacy; transport and mobility; health, work and leisure. The second part turns to the wider social and political setting, including estates and social hierarchy, famine, rural and urban labour, the market economy, and the political movements of the late imperial period. The review draws on 224 sources, including monographs, journal articles, theses, ethnographic field reports, museum collections and contemporary statistics. Throughout, it separates what the evidence shows from what it cannot show, and warns against generalising findings from one region, ethnic group or social class to the whole empire. Appendices provide a chronology and a glossary of Russian terms. Available in Turkish (original) and English. Note: AI tools (Anthropic Claude and OpenAI ChatGPT) assisted with literature search, drafting and editing. The author defined the scope, checked the sources and citations, and takes full responsibility for the content.

Addressing the onboarding barriers in Web3 machine-to-machine (M2M) and AI agent commerce—namely manual seed phrase management, interactive browser wallet requirements, heterogeneous testnet faucet hunting latency, and persistent bearer token vulnerabilities—this specification discloses a unified, single-endpoint provisioning protocol operating in under four seconds (T_onboard < 4.0s): (1) Single-seed Ed25519 deterministic key derivation across three heterogeneous cryptographic curves and address encodings (Bech32m SynapticChain L1, Base58 Solana Devnet, and Base58Check Ripple Classic XRPL); (2) Root-authorized administrative minting of non-transferable soulbound identity credentials (SynIdentityNFT) bound to the agent's Layer-1 address; (3) On-chain Trusted Agent Protocol (TAP) registration in AgentRegistry enforcing automated daily and per-transaction spending limit governance; (4) Synchronous heterogeneous tri-rail capital disbursement from custodian reserves funding native gas (0.5 SYN), working capital (0.5 sUSD), Solana lamports (0.01 SOL), and XRPL drops (2.0 XRP) in a single atomic flow; and (5) Issuance of an on-chain compute license (McpLicenseNFT v3) authorizing access to an 11-server Model Context Protocol (MCP) fleet via six detached Ed25519 request headers binding an ephemeral challenge, tool identifier, and agent identity (sha256('challenge:tool:agent')), eliminating static API keys and persistent credential theft.

Modern sport combines human skill, physical preparation and increasingly sophisticated technological support. Exercise technology may be understood as the practical application of scientific knowledge, equipment, digital systems and analytical procedures to improve exercise prescription, athlete monitoring, performance assessment and sporting environments. Technology can be as simple as improved footwear or electronic timing and as complex as motion-capture systems, wearable sensors, artificial intelligence and integrated athlete-management platforms.The importance of technology lies not only in producing more information but in helping practitioners convert information into useful decisions. A coach may use video to identify a technical error, a physiologist may use heart-rate or oxygen consumption data to quantify internal load, and a strength and conditioning professional may use velocity measurements to regulate resistance training. The value of each tool depends on validity, reliability, correct interpretation and its relevance to the athlete’s needs.

documents.abstract: This study investigates socioeconomic and rural–urban disparities in access to artificial intelligence (AI) among engineering students enrolled following the TVET path in Bangladesh. We further analyse how socioeconomic status (SES) and geographic location affect access to AI tools and their impact on academic performance. Using primary survey data from diploma engineering students, the study applies a probit model to evaluate AI access and a multivariable linear regression model to assess the influence of AI usage on academic outcomes. Results demonstrate that students from higher-SES backgrounds and especially those who come from urban backgrounds achieve academic performance levels 20% higher, likely due to increased access to technology and a more supportive educational environment. Conversely, students from lower-income and rural backgrounds experience restricted access and lower academic achievement. These findings underscore the necessity for targeted policy interventions, including subsidized access and improved rural digital infrastructure, to foster inclusive educational outcomes.

Existing spatial reasoning benchmarks mainly test spatial perception: reading off relations already visible in the input. Yet real-world spatial intelligence demands predictive spatial reasoning: constructing a scene from observations, anticipating how an intervention changes it, and reasoning about the unseen outcome. We introduce SpaceCast-Bench, the first benchmark to directly and diagnostically evaluate this capability. Built around an observe-transform-infer framework, its 3,862 questions from 182 real-world scenes span 16 task types at three levels: static perception, local prediction, and global prediction, progressively requiring scene understanding, spatial state updating, and relational inference over unobserved outcomes. Evaluating 21 models exposes a stark gap: the strongest model reaches only 58.0% against 87.2% human performance, while spatially specialized models remain near random chance. Controlled analyses further reveal that bridge views are critical for integrating distributed observations, and that explicit 3D evidence benefits models more reliably than generated outcome images or videos. Fine-tuning on our programmatically generated data lifts Qwen3-VL-4B from 34.0% to 65.7% with macro-average gains across six out-of-domain benchmarks.

In the context of rapid digital transformation, modernizing commercial bank credit services has become a strategic priority. This article examines key directions for reforming credit mechanisms through digital technologies and data-driven solutions, aiming to optimize lending processes, reduce operational costs, and improve customer experience. Particular attention is given to Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Big Data analytics in automated credit scoring and risk assessment. The study also analyzes end-to-end digital lending channels, open banking APIs for real-time decision-making, and the potential of blockchain and smart contracts to enhance transparency and security. Key challenges, including cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and data privacy, are discussed alongside practical solutions. The paper concludes with strategic recommendations to strengthen banks' competitiveness, improve credit portfolio quality, and expand financial inclusion.

Machine-generated decision claims — the outputs of large language models (LLMs) in high-stakes contexts — are narratives: fluent, plausible, and structurally incomplete. This report specifies a deterministic, offline, model-agnostic method for auditing the structure of decision claims: (i) a formal decision-structure language with a machine-checkable grammar and a validator that rejects conclusion-bearing, recommendation-bearing, ranking, and optimisation text by construction (19 diagnostic codes); (ii) a five-operator audit pipeline (narrative stripping, implicit-assumption surfacing, fragility assessment, causal-chain synchronisation, state anchoring) with an explicit severity model in which only structural absence — never quantitative opinion — may block an audit; and (iii) a tamper-evident, reproducible evidence chain whose integrity any third party can re-verify offline. A structural taxonomy of decision claims — anchored / floating / opaque / hollow — is defined independently of factual truth and measured by a fixed procedure. The method does not evaluate whether a claim is true; it records whether the claim declares the assumptions it depends on and the responses it commits to when those assumptions fail — the evidence layer required by record-keeping, transparency, and human-oversight obligations of high-risk AI governance regimes. 摘要 —— 大模型在高风险场景下输出的"决策主张"本质是叙事:流畅、可信、但结构不完整。本文给出结构完整性与证据属性这一正交维度的确定性、离线、与模型无关的审计方法:一门可机器校验的决策结构语言(19 条诊断码,按构造拒绝结论/建议/排序/优化类表述);五算子审计流水线(叙事剥离、内隐假设透视、脆弱性闩锁、因果链同步、状态锚定),其严重度模型规定:只有结构性缺失可以阻断,量化意见不能;可防篡改、可复现的证据链,任何第三方可离线重算。另给出与事实真伪无关、可按固定程序测量的结构分类法(锚定/浮置/不透明/空洞)。方法不判断主张真假,只记录"该主张是否声明了所依赖的假设、以及假设失效时所承诺的分支响应"。 Contents: (1) paper.pdf — the report, Version 1.0, 2026-10-09; (2) paper.md — Markdown source; (3) second-perspective-2026-10-09.zip — complete source snapshot of the reference implementation (Global Cognitive Audit Engine GCAE v2.0.0; Second-Perspective Decision Structure Language, Standard 2026.1; verification suite); (4) verify-output.log — full verification output at snapshot time. documents.abstract: [Background.] Multi-step web workflows, such as comparing offers across portals, cost people much time. Scripts must be written for each site and break when pages change; agents built on large language models can pursue a goal stated in natural language on unseen sites. Current agents depend on site-specific interaction, spend many tokens on large pages and redundant steps, use expensive vision models at every step, do not reuse earlier work, and give users few safeguards. [Objective.] This thesis develops and evaluates a generalized, trustworthy and human-centred web agent for enterprise-relevant tasks, with five objectives: generalization, a bounded cost, intent reasoning and task decomposition, knowing when to involve a person, and safety, security and privacy. [Approach.] Each limitation leads to a design principle and a component. Structured DOM preprocessing represents any page as site-independent records, notes what it could not read in a coverage manifest, and gives the model only a compact extract. URL optimization shortens interactions, and parallel agents handle the subtasks of a decomposed goal. Selective multimodal reasoning calls a vision model only when text is not enough. Agentic context engineering reuses experience through curated playbooks and a memory of earlier runs. A policy layer separates permitting an action from executing it and hands control to a person at logins and approvals, and a completion is accepted only when stored evidence supports it. [Evaluation.] On 1,656 scored tasks from WebVoyager, Online-Mind2Web, WebArena and Odysseys, run with grok-4-1-fast-reasoning (Grok) on live sites and DeepSeek-V4-Flash on WebArena, strict success is 69.7% to 95.9%. On the 229 Online-Mind2Web tasks every variant reached, the full architecture on Grok solves 86.5% against 65.1% for the same model given only the DOM and a screenshot, and 69.4% against 40.8% of the hard ones, at about six times the cost per completed task. Without its completion check, wrong completions rise from 2.8% to 15.3%; without vision, success falls by 11 points. Under Grok a task costs $0.10–$0.20 for routine browsing and up to $1.54 for long research ($3.56 under DeepSeek); GPT-6.1 Sol matches Grok at six times the cost. In a pilot, six people checked a saved run in a median of 3.5 minutes and accepted 10 of 12 answers unchanged. [Conclusion.] A suitable architecture lets an inexpensive model succeed on multistep web tasks across very different sites, where the same model without it solves far fewer. Evidence handling, safety policy and human control belong to the runtime, so they carry over to stronger models. Left open are the effect of memory alone, false completions on long tasks, and attacks on the safeguards.

Objective: To characterise the landscape of surgical artificial intelligence (AI) devices approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Background: AI has the potential to improve surgical pathways, offering capability across screening, diagnosis, decision support, and intraoperative care. Despite this, real-world adoption remains limited. Regulatory approval serves as a key step in clinical translation but is influenced by challenges in evidence generation, safety, bias, transparency, and implementation. Consequently, the characteristics, evidence base, and functional roles of FDA-cleared surgical AI devices remain incompletely defined. Methods: FDA-cleared AI/machine learning medical devices were systematically screened for surgical relevance up to July 2025. Eligible devices were extracted for clinical application, underlying AI technology, evidence quality, and regulatory pathway. Devices were categorised using an adapted descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive framework, and predicate networks were evaluated for risk of predicate creep. Analyses were performed in R. Results: A total of 314 devices (25.1%) had surgical applications. Most were imaging-based devices and mapped to general surgery (24.8%), orthopaedic surgery (18.2%), neurosurgery (17.2%), and cardiac surgery (10.8%). The majority of devices were descriptive (50.6%) or diagnostic (40.4%), with relatively few predictive (1.3%) or prescriptive (7.6%) applications. Clinical validation was predominantly based on retrospective or bench studies, with only 5.1% supported by higher-quality prospective evidence. The premarket notification 510(k) pathway accounted for 95.2% of approvals. Among these, 37.5% demonstrated a high risk of predicate creep, reflecting substantial differences in intended use or technological characteristics compared with predicate devices. Conclusion: FDA-approved surgical AI devices are currently dominated by imaging-based diagnostic tools. The widespread reliance on the 510(k) pathway and the observed prevalence of predicate creep highlight important considerations for regulatory evaluation. As AI applications expand toward predictive and interventional roles, improved evidence transparency and robust assessment of device equivalence will be essential to support safe clinical adoption.

documents.abstract: Abstract Conversational Large Language Model (LLM) agents, deployed quickly, have exposed unprecedented opportunities for personal information, from health data to financial information, to biometric identifiers. This critical enlightenment review investigates general privacy dangers in each of five areas: data leakage and memorization, adversarial extraction and prompt injection, inference and re-identification, surveillance and profiling and regulatory governance breakdown. We trace privacy threats from static data breaches to dynamic ones that have become part of an architecture, associated with neural memorization and contextual inference (2020–2026), using expert selection of primary studies and technical benchmark sources. Upon close examination, technical mitigations (differential privacy, federated learning and machine unlearning) prove successful to some extent when operating in controlled environments, but fail to provide complete protection in conversational environments. We combine classical theory on Privacy-Preserving Data Publishing (PPDP) with emerging threats from LLMs, and present a conflict-of-evidence analysis which reveals that privacy protections are particularly effective in structured environments with low risks, or with consumers actively responsible for maintaining them, but fail to adequately protect privacy in high-stakes domains without human control, technical safeguards, and legal liability. We systematically examine and analyze a dimension that has not been studied sufficiently: risks of data deletion and editing illusion, and introduce techniques for unlearning machines that leave behind traces that can be exploited by adversarial reconstruction. We support the multi-layered mitigation framework of PPDP principles, technical safeguards, and governance reform.

documents.abstract: Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada zamonaviy ta’lim tizimiga sun’iy intellekt (SI) texnologiyalarini integratsiya qilishning konseptual va amaliy jihatlari tadqiq etilgan. Ta’lim jarayonida SI vositalari, jumladan, ChatGPT, adaptiv ta’lim platformalari va avtomatlashtirilgan baholash tizimlaridan foydalanishning ijobiyjihatlari - ta’limni personallashtirish, vaqtni tejash va inklyuzivlikni ta’minlash, shuningdek, salbiy jihatlari - akademik halollik bilan bog‘liq muammolar, kognitiv passivlik va raqamli tengsizlik tizimli ravishda tahlil qilingan. Tadqiqot metodologiyasi sifat va miqdoriy ma’lumotlarning qiyosiy tahliliga asoslangan. Tadqiqot natijalari SI texnologiyalaridan samarali foydalanish ta’lim jarayonining natijadorligini oshirish imkonini berishini, biroq ulardan nazoratsiz va maqsadsiz foydalanish talabalarning mustaqil va tanqidiy fikrlash ko‘nikmalarining rivojlanishiga salbiy ta’sir ko‘rsatishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatadi. Shuningdek, SI texnologiyalaridan foydalanish bilan bog‘liq ehtimoliy salbiy oqibatlarni minimallashtirish hamda ularni ta’lim jarayoniga pedagogik jihatdan maqsadga muvofiq integratsiya qilish bo‘yicha strategik tavsiyalar ishlab chiqilgan. Аннотация. В статье исследуются концептуальные и практические аспекты интеграции технологий искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в современную систему образования. Проведён системный анализ положительных аспектов использования инструментов ИИ в образовательном процессе, включая ChatGPT, адаптивные образовательные платформы и автоматизированные системы оценивания, таких как персонализация обучения, экономия времени и обеспечение инклюзивности, а также потенциальных негативных аспектов - проблем академической добросовестности, когнитивной пассивности и цифрового неравенства. Методология исследования основана на сравнительном анализе качественных и количественных данных. Результаты исследования показывают, что эффективное использование технологий ИИ способствуетповышению результативности образовательного процесса, однако их неконтролируемое и нецелевое применение может негативно влиять на развитие навыков самостоятельного и критического мышления студентов. Кроме того, разработаны стратегические рекомендации по минимизации возможных негативных последствий использования ИИ и его педагогически целесообразной интеграции в образовательный процесс. Abstract. This article examines the conceptual and practical aspects of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into modern education systems. It provides a systematic analysis of both the benefits of using AI tools in education, including ChatGPT, adaptive learning platforms, and automated assessmentsystems, such as personalized learning, time efficiency, and enhanced inclusivity, and the potential challenges associated with their use, including academic integrity concerns, cognitive passivity, and digital inequality. The research methodology is based on a comparative analysis of qualitative and quantitative data. The findings indicate that the effective use of AI technologies can enhance the overall effectiveness of the educational process; however, uncontrolled and purposeless use may adversely affect the development of students’ independent and critical thinking skills. The article also proposes strategicrecommendations for minimizing the potential negative consequences associated with AI use and ensuring its pedagogically appropriate integration into the educational process.

documents.abstract: Introduction: ESA’s missions produce vast scientific data and thousands of publications annually. Identifying those that truly analyze mission data is essential but manual review is unfeasible. TACTICIAN uses NLP, ML, DL, and LLMs to automate extraction and classification of mission-related knowledge. Methodology and Relation Extraction: The TACTICIAN system presents an integrated approach for converting unstructured scientific literature into structured knowledge that is directly connected to specific space science missions. By leveraging a combination of syntactic and semantic Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, the framework effectively extracts and organizes mission-relevant information. This process includes several key components: Part-ofSpeech (POS) tagging, which identifies grammatical structures; dependency parsing to elucidate relationships between words; named-entity recognition to pinpoint mission-specific instruments, targets, and observation identifiers; temporal expression extraction to capture relevant timeframes; and entity-based summarization that synthesizes core findings. Collectively, these methods enable TACTICIAN to detect crucial mission characteristics such as instruments, targets, wavelengths, observation identifiers, and predicates indicating how scientific data is utilized, thus facilitating the transformation of complex scientific texts into actionable, mission-linked datasets. Scalable LLM Classification and Reflection: Recent advancements in the TACTICIAN project emphasize the use of classification pipelines built upon Large Language Models (LLMs). These pipelines are specifically designed to operate without the need for missionspecific training, enabling robust performance even when applied to new missions or novel datasets. By employing zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies, the system can effectively classify publications and extract relevant information without extensive prior training. The integration of automatic summarization and structured JSON outputs ensures that the extracted knowledge is organized and easily accessible, while delivering results that are on par with the most effective Deep Learning (DL) models. A notable feature of this approach is LLM reflection. In this process, the model initially generates a prediction based on the input, then formulates a probing question to test the validity or depth of its response and finally reassesses its answer considering this selfquestioning. This reflective methodology enhances both the accuracy and the explainability of the classification outcomes, making the pipeline not only powerful but also transparent and trustworthy for missionlinked literature analysis. Conclusion: The TACTICIAN system leverages advanced Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Large Language Model technologies to reliably classify space science literature, accurately extract mission-specific knowledge,and establish connections between publications and observational archives. Traditional ML and DL approaches achieve high accuracy in organizing missionlinked information, while LLM-based methods offer scalable, mission-agnostic solutions ideal for analyzing future space mission literature. These capabilities directly support the European Space Agency’s goals by enabling scientific impact assessment, promoting open-science reproducibility, improving intelligent archive services, and laying the groundwork for expanding multimodal and agentic AI applications in the space domain. Acknowledgments: This work has received funding from the European Space Agency (ESA Contract No 4000128429/19/ES/JD).

Annotatsiya. Ushbu maqolada oliy ta’lim muassasalarida tahsil olayotgantalabalarning ingliz tilida og‘zaki nutq (Speaking) ko‘nikmalarini rivojlantirishdazamonaviy raqamli platformalardan foydalanish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi.Xususan, Cambly, HelloTalk, Speak va ELSA Speak kabi platformalarningtalabalarning og‘zaki nutqi, talaffuzi, kommunikativ kompetensiyasi hamda ingliztilida erkin muloqot qilish qobiliyatini rivojlantirishdagi o‘rni yoritiladi. Raqamlitexnologiyalardan foydalanish talabalarga auditoriyadan tashqari vaqtda ham ingliztilida muntazam mashq qilish, real suhbatlarda yoki sun’iy intellektga asoslanganmuloqot jarayonlarida ishtirok etish hamda individual qayta aloqa olish imkoniniberadi.Maqolada mazkur platformalardan samarali foydalanish uchun o‘qituvchitomonidan maqsadli topshiriqlar ishlab chiqish, muntazam og‘zaki nutq amaliyotinitashkil etish va tegishli baholash mezonlarini belgilash zarurligi asoslanadi.Tadqiqot natijalari zamonaviy raqamli platformalarni an’anaviy ta’lim jarayonibilan uyg‘unlashtirish talabalarning ingliz tilida og‘zaki nutq ko‘nikmalarinirivojlantirish va muloqot jarayonida o‘ziga bo‘lgan ishonchini oshirishga ijobiyta’sir ko‘rsatishi mumkinligini ko‘rsatadi. Abstract. This article analyzes the potential of modern digital platforms fordeveloping English-speaking skills among university students. In particular, itexamines the role of platforms such as Cambly, HelloTalk, Speak, and ELSA Speakin improving students’ oral communication, pronunciation, communicativecompetence, and ability to communicate fluently in English. The use of digitaltechnologies enables students to practice English regularly outside the classroom,participate in real-life or artificial intelligence-based conversations, and receiveindividualized feedback. The article emphasizes the importance of developing purposeful tasks,organizing regular speaking practice, and establishing appropriate assessmentcriteria under the guidance of a teacher to ensure the effective use of these platforms.The findings suggest that integrating modern digital platforms with traditionallanguage instruction can positively contribute to the development of students’English-speaking skills and increase their confidence in using English forcommunication. Аннотaция. В статье анализируются возможности использованиясовременных цифровых платформ для развития навыков устной речи наанглийском языке у студентов высших образовательных учреждений. Особоевнимание уделяется таким платформам, как Cambly, HelloTalk, Speak и ELSASpeak, а также их роли в совершенствовании устной речи, произношения,коммуникативной компетенции и способности студентов свободно общатьсяна английском языке. Использование цифровых технологий позволяетстудентам регулярно практиковать английский язык во внеаудиторное время,участвовать в реальных диалогах или коммуникативных ситуaциях,основанных на технологиях искусственного интеллекта, а также получатьиндивидуальную обратную связь.В статье обосновывается необходимость разработки преподавателемцеленаправленных заданий, организaции регулярной разговорной практики иопределения соответствующих критериев оценивания для эффективногоиспользования данных платформ. Результаты исследования показывают, чтоинтегрaция современных цифровых платформ с традиционным процессомобучения иностранному языку может положительно способствовать развитиюнавыков устной речи студентов и повышению их уверенности прииспользовании английского языка в процессе коммуникaции.

Introduction Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition for which cognitive assessment can be time-consuming, resource intensive, and subject to interpretation. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers potential advantages in accuracy, efficiency, and usability, but human-centered factors influencing acceptance remain insufficiently examined. Methods This study examined healthcare and education professionals' perceptions of AI-based versus traditional cognitive assessment for ASD using a multi-method analytical framework. A final sample of 77 participants was analyzed after three outliers were removed. The analysis integrated PLS-SEM, fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), PLSpredict, and robustness analyses to examine structural relationships, configurational pathways, predictive relevance, mediation, and moderation. Results AI-based assessment was perceived as more accurate, time-efficient, and user-friendly than traditional assessment. Perceived AI-based accuracy significantly predicted AI acceptance ( β = 0.412, p < .001), while ease of use partially mediated the accuracy–acceptance relationship (VAF = 55.3%). Prior AI exposure and professional role influenced the relationships examined. fsQCA identified three configurations associated with high AI acceptance. PLSpredict indicated out-of-sample predictive relevance (Q²predict = 0.410). Discussion The findings indicate that perceived accuracy, ease of use, and time efficiency are important dimensions of professionals' acceptance of AI-based cognitive assessment. The study integrates TAM and UTAUT2 with cognitive-load and psychometric perspectives and provides evidence relevant to AI implementation, professional training, workflow design, and ethical governance in ASD assessment.

documents.abstract: Purpose Existing research on gamified flipped classrooms (GFC) has often treated engagement as an overall outcome, leaving limited understanding of how behavioral, cognitive and emotional engagement change over time. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Merrill’s First Principles of Instruction (FPI), this three-wave quasi-experimental mixed-methods study examined engagement trajectories among undergraduate software engineering students in gamified and traditional flipped classrooms across a 16-week semester. Findings Questionnaire data and post-intervention interviews showed limited and non-sustained differences between the two instructional conditions. More importantly, behavioral engagement remained comparatively stable and cognitive engagement showed only limited temporal variation, whereas emotional engagement was relatively more sensitive to time. Qualitative findings indicated that behavioral engagement was largely maintained by instructional routines and task requirements, cognitive engagement was shaped by pragmatic task-oriented strategies and emotional engagement was more responsive to changing course experiences. Research limitations/implications These findings demonstrate that engagement dimensions do not necessarily develop uniformly within the same instructional environment and support a dimension-sensitive approach to GFC design. Originality/value This study extends GFC research by moving beyond overall or short-term measures of student engagement to examine the semester-long trajectories of behavioral, cognitive and emotional engagement simultaneously. The findings show that these engagement dimensions do not develop uniformly: behavioral engagement remains relatively stable and cognitive engagement shows limited temporal variation, whereas emotional engagement is comparatively more time-sensitive. By integrating SDT with Merrill’s FPI and combining three-wave quantitative data with qualitative explanations, the study provides a dimension-sensitive and temporally informed understanding of how gamification operates within structured flipped classrooms.

Purpose This paper argues that generative artificial intelligence (AI) has forced a reckoning with a long-standing inadequacy in the temporal assumptions that have structured educational thought since the Enlightenment. It introduces post-linear epistemology as a framework for understanding how knowledge functions when learning is no longer adequately modelled as movement through a temporal sequence and develops concrete implications for curriculum design, assessment and teacher practice. Design/methodology/approach The paper is conceptual. It synthesizes scholarship on complexity in education, non-linear learning, technological acceleration, futures studies and critical artificial intelligence in education and uses this synthesis to specify the conditions under which a post-linear account of educational knowledge becomes necessary. Findings The paper identifies three interrelated shifts that, on this account, characterize the post-linear condition and are proposed here as claims for further examination rather than as established findings. First, chronologically ordered curriculum sequences are argued to be no longer adequate as the default architecture of educational design – though not as the only legitimate one. Second, cumulative derivation is argued to be increasingly displaced, in AI-mediated contexts, by probabilistic and relational forms of knowledge production. Third, temporal literacy – the capacity to identify when information was produced, how it has drifted and what time-frame it presupposes – is proposed as a distinct educational capacity, with three specifiable components, that these conditions make newly necessary. Research limitations/implications The paper is conceptual, not empirical. The claims about how recursive AI use affects student work and about whether temporal literacy can actually be taught and measured are presented as hypotheses for design-based research, not as findings. The framework is meant to make those questions easier to investigate, not to answer them. Practical implications Three changes follow. Curriculum design should look at which prerequisite sequences are actually necessary and which are inherited habit. Pedagogy should teach temporal literacy directly, using provenance critique, drift mapping and positioning essays, instead of treating it as a by-product of other work. Assessment should measure how students locate and situate knowledge, not just what they can reproduce. Social implications AI-generated text routinely blends sources from different periods into a single fluent voice. That makes the question of whose perspectives get amplified, and whose get smoothed away, a public concern rather than a specialist one. Temporal literacy is one of the capacities through which an ordinary reader can interrogate AI-mediated text for what it has left out. Originality/value Other accounts of non-linear learning (complexity theory, connectivism, postdigital thought) already cover much of what AI intensifies. None of them was built for one specific thing: AI generation flattens the temporal markers that normally tell sources apart. This paper picks out that specific feature, names the literacy needed to read against it and turns the conceptual claim into concrete recommendations for curriculum, assessment and teacher practice.

Introduction Generative artificial intelligence has diffused rapidly among learners, but a question remains whether that reach becomes useful for learning or stalls at access. This distinction matters most where learners already have connectivity, so the barrier is no longer reaching the technology but converting access into learning use. Methods This study draws on a survey of 14,653 computer science learners across 166 countries, a population for whom first-level access is broadly shared. A two-part model separates whether an everyday user converts to any learning use from how widely converters then use the tool, estimated across World Bank income tiers. Results Everyday adoption is high across income levels and is not lower in poorer settings. The quantity that varies is conversion. Among everyday users, those in low-income countries are markedly less likely to convert to any learning use, at an odds ratio of 0.49 (95% CI 0.27, 0.90), while breadth among converters does not differ by income tier. A latent typology shows that disengaged learners are found across every income tier rather than in one region, and the association between AI use and self-rated proficiency is strongest where other support is weakest. Discussion The gap sits at the threshold of first learning use, not in the breadth beyond it. This article names the pattern the access-conversion gap and develops it as a measurable construct at the second and third levels of the digital divide. The findings describe a connected population of engaged learners, so the divide to address is in use, not access.

Classical theory assumes upon a human entrepreneur who bears uncertainty, exercises alertness and recognises opportunity. We examine what becomes of that assumption when artificial intelligence (AI) performs these issues. Defining AI as agentic systems built on large foundation models, we analyse how far such systems manifest core entrepreneurial attributes and where they reach fundamental limits. We propose the AI Entrepreneurial Agency Framework (AEAF), a four-level model organised along two conceptually independent dimensions: the autonomy of AI judgment and the degree of Knightian uncertainty in the task environment. Three falsifiable propositions theorise the redistribution of uncertainty and accountability, the intentionality boundary on opportunity framing and alertness, and the cognitive-computational re-conception of the individual–opportunity nexus. Incorporating Bayesian entrepreneurship, we specify where AI accelerates experimentation and where it cannot. A structured review of fourteen studies positions the AEAF as an integrated platform for this frontier, with implications for theory, strategy and AI governance.

documents.abstract: This study examines the impact of using artificial intelligence (AI) metacognitive scaffolds on the of university student's academic performance in Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt, while analyzing the mediating roles of learning self-efficacy, cognitive load, and intrinsic motivation. Using quantitative design, data collected from 436 students utilizing AI learning platforms through PLS-SEM, grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, Cognitive Load Theory, and Self-Determination Theory. Results confirmed all hypotheses, revealing that AIX significantly positively affects LSE, RCL, IIM, and AP. Critically, RCL emerged as the strongest predictor of AP, while LSE served as a crucial mediator through sequential pathways: AIX → LSE → RCL → AP and AIX → LSE → IIM→AP, the above findings provide an empirical justification for the implementation of AI technologies within the higher education institutions of the MENA region .
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: Against the backdrop that artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the labor market and occupational ecosystem, how college students build career preparation amid technological uncertainty has become a pressing question. Integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) with Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), this study constructs a research model in which AI acceptance is associated with career goal setting through AI trust and career confidence, and it examines the moderating role of intrinsic motivation. This study surveys undergraduate students in Chinese universities, obtaining 539 valid responses. The results show that (1) both performance expectancy and effort expectancy are positively associated with AI trust, with a stronger association for performance expectancy; (2) AI trust is positively associated with career confidence; (3) career confidence is positively associated with career goal setting; (4) AI trust and career confidence play a serial mediating role between performance expectancy, effort expectancy and career goal setting; (5) intrinsic motivation positively moderates the relationship between AI trust and career confidence, such that this association is stronger at higher levels of intrinsic motivation. These findings reveal how AI acceptance relates to college students’ career preparation and offer evidence for universities to implement AI literacy education and career counseling.

Conversational intelligent tutoring systems (CITS) have the potential to bring health education to low-income communities at scale. Although educational attainment is usually low, the health literacy spectrum within these communities can be wide. Therefore, special attention should be paid when designing and evaluating CITS within these communities. Visual, linguistic, subject matter, and cultural models must be considered. Moreover, evaluating CITS can be challenging. The instruments used to assess the impact of these systems must consider the levels of health literacy of the individuals who interact with them. In this work, we present a community-engaged design process of a breast cancer CITS for Latinas from low-income communities in Chicago. The system comprises an autonomous version and a wizard-of-Oz version—a system that appears to work autonomously to its users but is operated remotely by researchers to control for potential flaws in its artificial intelligence engine. Then, we present and contrast a case study of two women who interacted with the system. Although the two women in this paper would be traditionally grouped together for statistical analysis, the evaluations we obtained suggest that for one of them, the evaluation instruments do not seem to accurately capture her experiences interacting with the CITS. We conclude by highlighting the need for purposefully designed systems for low-income communities that rely on cultural models as well as language models and advocate for designing evaluation instruments that faithfully capture the experiences of all participants.

documents.abstract: Introduction This study aimed to examine the effect of individuals’ anxiety toward AI-based health technologies on their attitudes toward the use of telemedicine services and to determine the mediating role of online privacy perception in this relationship. Methods Designed within a quantitative research approach, the study employed a cross-sectional design. Data were collected through an online survey from 404 participants aged 18 years and older living in Istanbul, selected using convenience sampling. The Artificial Intelligence Anxiety Scale, the Telemedicine Service Attitude Scale, and the Online Privacy Perception Scale were used as data collection instruments. The reliability levels of the scales were found to be satisfactory. Results The findings showed that AI anxiety had a direct negative effect on attitudes toward telemedicine services, while also increasing online privacy perception. Online privacy perception negatively affected attitudes toward the use of telemedicine services. Mediation analysis indicated that online privacy perception had a significant and partial mediating role in the effect of AI anxiety on telemedicine use (β = −0.651; p < 0.001). Discussion The findings suggest that individuals’ psychological concerns and privacy-related perceptions are important determinants of the adoption of digital health services. Accordingly, reducing AI-related anxiety and strengthening privacy assurance may support more positive attitudes toward telemedicine services.

This study examined the effect of integrating ChatGPT with the Role-Play Technique on students’ speaking fluency and speaking confidence. The study was motivated by students’ difficulties in speaking English, particularly their limited fluency and low confidence during classroom speaking activities. A mixed-method research design was employed involving 35 eleventh-grade students at SMAS Nurul Iman Tanjung Morawa during the 2025/2026 academic year. The participants consisted of 17 students in the experimental group and 18 students in the control group. The experimental group used ChatGPT as a rehearsal partner before participating in face-to-face role-play activities, while the control group participated in conventional role-play without AI assistance. Data were collected through speaking tests, classroom observations, and a speaking confidence questionnaire. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk normality test, the Mann–Whitney U test, and effect size analysis using SPSS version 26. The findings showed a significant difference between the experimental and control groups in speaking fluency and speaking confidence. The Mann–Whitney U test produced significance values of 0.000 for both variables. The effect sizes were 0.87 for speaking fluency and 0.74 for speaking confidence, indicating large effects. The observation and questionnaire findings also showed greater participation, willingness to communicate, and confidence among students in the experimental group. The findings indicate that integrating ChatGPT as a rehearsal partner with the Role-Play Technique provided a supportive approach to developing students’ English speaking performance.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is generating unprecedented technological opportunities while raising profound ethical, anthropological, and social challenges. This article examines the role of the Catholic Church in shaping AI ethics within the tension between technological progress and a personalist understanding of the human person. The study employs a hermeneutical approach and critical analysis of the scholarly literature and key documents of the Church’s Magisterium, including Gaudium et Spes, Laudato si’, Laudate Deum, and the Rome Call for AI Ethics. It also compares Catholic ethical reflection with selected secular frameworks, namely the OECD Principles on Artificial Intelligence, the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, and the European Union AI Act. The findings indicate that Catholic reflection on AI is grounded in an integral personalist anthropology that emphasises human dignity, the common good, moral responsibility, and the relational nature of the person as fundamental criteria for evaluating technology. While secular regulatory models primarily focus on safety, transparency, and accountability, the Catholic perspective contributes a deeper anthropological and theological dimension rooted in the concept of imago Dei. The article proposes a model of ‘personalist ethics of co-creation’ that integrates contemporary AI ethics standards with a Christian vision of human responsibility. Such an approach may complement existing legal and technical regulations and promote a more human-centred development and use of AI.

documents.abstract: Climate change is intensifying water insecurity across Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), threatening agricultural productivity, ecosystem integrity, and sustainable livelihoods. Climate-smart water management (CSWM) has consequently emerged as an important approach for strengthening water security and climate resilience. This scoping review maps the existing evidence on the convergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Nature-Based Solutions (NbS), and adaptive governance in supporting climate-smart water management across SSA. Guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), a systematic search of peer-reviewed and grey literature published between 2000 and 2026 identified 1265 records, of which 15 studies met the inclusion criteria. The review found that the evidence base remains limited and fragmented but reflects growing scholarly interest in integrating technological, ecological, and governance approaches to climate adaptation. The included studies reported AI applications primarily in remote sensing, predictive analytics, climate forecasting, decision support systems, and irrigation management, while NbS focused on watershed restoration, agroforestry, wetland conservation, rainwater harvesting, and ecosystem-based adaptation. Adaptive governance emerged as a cross-cutting theme emphasizing stakeholder participation, knowledge co-production, institutional coordination, and adaptive learning. Several studies highlighted the potential complementarities among AI, NbS, and governance, although few empirically examined their integrated implementation. Recurring implementation challenges included digital infrastructure disparities, limited technical and institutional capacity, financing constraints, fragmented governance arrangements, and unequal access to AI technologies. The review also identified substantial geographical and empirical evidence gaps, particularly regarding implementation effectiveness, scalability, equity, and long-term outcomes. Collectively, the findings highlight the need for interdisciplinary, context-specific, and implementation-oriented research to support equitable and climate-resilient water management policies and practices across Sub-Saharan Africa.
